prompt: To graph $y = 3x + 2$, you plot the start $(0, 2)$, then move right $1$. What $y$-value do you land on?
hint: The slope tells you how much the line rises each time you move $1$ unit to the right.

hints.text: The slope tells you how much the line rises each time you move $1$ unit to the right.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Start at the y-intercept $(0, 2)$. Moving right $1$ climbs by the slope $3$: $2 + 3 = 5$. The slope IS the step size.
The slope is $3$, so moving right $1$ from $(0, 2)$ raises the height by $3$. Add that to the starting height of $2$.
$2 + 3 = 5$, so you land on the point $(1, 5)$ and the $y$-value is $5$.

explanation: To graph a line in slope-intercept form, plot the $y$-intercept first and then use the slope as rise over run.
The slope $3$ is the same as $\frac{3}{1}$, which means go up $3$ for each $1$ to the right.
Starting from $(0, 2)$, moving right $1$ and up $3$ lands on $(1, 5)$, so the $y$-value is $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Just plug in
steps: Moving right $1$ from $x = 0$ puts you at $x = 1$.
$y = 3 \times 1 + 2 = 5$ — the graph move and the formula agree.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Moving up by 1 — copying the run instead of the slope — lands on 3 instead of 5.
The slope 3 is the STAIR HEIGHT: right 1, up 3. From (0, 2) that is (1, 5), so y = 5.
